facts.label: scripture
facts.quote: Hanuman goes and informs about safety and impending arrival of Rama to Bharata who was about to jump in fire.
facts.text: In the Kamba Ramayanam, Bharata prepared a blazing pyre and was circumambulating it to immolate himself when Hanuman appeared, physically extinguished the fire, and delivered news of Rama's return.

facts.label: scripture
facts.quote: बैठे देखि कुसासन जटा मुकुट कृस गात। राम राम रघुपति जपत स्रवत नयन जलजात॥
facts.text: In Goswami Tulsidas's Ramcharitmanas, Bharata was sinking into desolation on the final day of exile before Hanuman arrived disguised as a Brahmin to halt his despair and deliver Rama's message.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: In continuation of last year's work which was taken up under the project called 'Archaeology of the Ramayana Sites', excavation was resumed under Professor B. B. Lal...
facts.text: In 1975, the Archaeological Survey of India inaugurated the national excavation project 'Archaeology of the Ramayana Sites' led by former Director General B.B. Lal to excavate Ayodhya, Nandigram, Sringaverapura, Bharadwaj Ashram, and Chitrakoot.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: Nandigram is located on the northern bank... NBPW was found at Chitrakuta and Nandigram.
facts.source_name: Archaeological Survey of India, Indian Archaeology 1976-77 Review
facts.text: Archaeological investigations at Nandigram, situated approximately 15 kilometers south of Ayodhya at modern Bharat Kund, yielded pottery sherds of Northern Black Polished Ware signifying an early historic settlement.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: A detailed excavation yielded archaeologic material belonging to seven different cultural periods in a total deposit of nearly 9 m below the top surface.
facts.text: Excavations conducted by the Archaeological Survey of India at the Ramayana-linked site of Sringaverapura revealed a massive kiln-fired brick tank complex extending across a stratigraphic cultural deposit of nearly nine metres.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: The results of the excavation have revealed cultural deposits from the Northern Black Polished Ware (NBPW) period onwards through Shunga, Kushan, Gupta, Post-Gupta, Rajput, and Medieval periods.
facts.text: In 2003, the Archaeological Survey of India documented continuous cultural stratification at the ancient mound of Ayodhya dating from the Northern Black Polished Ware period of the early first millennium BCE up through medieval occupation levels.

facts.label: disputed
facts.quote: Prof. Shereen F. Ratnagar basically sought to contradict Dr. B.B. Lal's observation about Ayodhya based on his excavation thereat made in 1976-77 and supported the book written by Prof. D. Mandal criticising Dr. B.B. Lal's report.
facts.text: Archaeologists and historians remain divided over epic archaeology, with B.B. Lal claiming that correlated Northern Black Polished Ware strata support a historical kernel for the Ramayana, while critics such as D. Mandal and Shereen Ratnagar argue that identifying generic ceramic horizons with epic narratives lacks scientific rigor.

facts.label: legend
facts.quote: Bharat Kund, also known as Nandigram, is traditionally venerated as the hermitage where Bharata awaited Rama and prepared to sacrifice himself in fire before Hanuman's intervention.
facts.text: Local oral lore at Bharat Kund maintains that Bharata had already lit the pyre and was moments away from leaping into the flames when Hanuman's shout from the sky halted him.
